sections.summary: Conditional sentences express hypothetical situations and their consequences.
rules: Zero conditional: If + present, present (general truths)
First conditional: If + present, will + base (real future possibility)
Second conditional: If + past simple, would + base (unreal present)
Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle (unreal past)
examples: If you heat water to 100°C, it boils. (zero - scientific fact)
If it rains tomorrow, I will stay home. (first - possible future)
If I had a million dollars, I would travel the world. (second - unreal present)
If I had studied harder, I would have passed. (third - unreal past)

commonMistakes.wrong: If I will see him, I will tell him.
commonMistakes.correct: If I see him, I will tell him.
commonMistakes.explanation: First conditional: use present simple in if-clause, not "will"

commonMistakes.wrong: If I would be rich, I would buy a house.
commonMistakes.correct: If I were rich, I would buy a house.
commonMistakes.explanation: Second conditional: use past simple in if-clause, not "would"

quiz.question: If she ___ (study) harder, she will pass the exam.
quiz.explanation: First conditional: present simple in if-clause

quiz.question: If I ___ (be) you, I would apologize.
quiz.explanation: Second conditional: use "were" for all persons in formal English

sections.summary: The passive voice emphasizes the action or receiver rather than the doer.
rules: Use when doer is unknown, unimportant, or obvious
Can be used in all tenses
Add "by" to mention the doer (if necessary)
examples: The car was stolen last night. (doer unknown)
English is spoken in many countries. (doer obvious)
The letter will be sent tomorrow. (focus on action)
The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci. (famous doer mentioned)

commonMistakes.explanation: Use past participle (written), not past simple (wrote)

commonMistakes.correct: The house is being built now.
commonMistakes.explanation: Present continuous passive: is/are being + past participle

quiz.question: A new hospital ___ (build) in our town next year.
quiz.explanation: Future passive: will be + past participle
